gates.reason: No substantiated fraud/diversion or observed minority abuse. Unmodified audit is positive; RPT and disclosure reconciliation remains open.
Audited core statements usable with explicit conversion-period, comparative-reclassification and cash-flow-sign corrections; acquisition/capital-return bridge remains incomplete.
No audited undrawn facility; actual October cash/availability not verified; base/bear cash gaps even under assumed bank continuity. No observed default claimed.
Official market evidence available, but ESM-I/ST, 600-share lot, circuits, recentlot-discretecapacity and missing bid/ask depth limit implementation.

GOV.reason: Unmodified audits and reported use of IPO proceeds support adequate conduct. The related-party remuneration line and cash-flow presentation require reconciliation.
GOV.contrary_evidence: No substantiated fraud, diversion or current default was found. An unmodified audit is positive evidence, not proof of zero governance risk.
GOV.anchor: 5–6 mixed/adequate band, lower point. No adverse-integrity override.
GOV.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

MOAT.reason: Contract-farmer relationships, traceability and food-customer qualifications have practical value. Reitzel demonstrates similar capability, and buyer concentration limits pricing freedom.
MOAT.contrary_evidence: Growing exports and long farmer relationships support repeat business, but do not establish persistent excess returns.
MOAT.anchor: 5–6 useful but contestable advantage, lower point.
MOAT.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

REV.reason: A 33.6980% three-year comparable India export CAGR starts at 9. FY26 exports grew 20.14%, rather than the perimeter-mixed consolidated 34.59%.
REV.contrary_evidence: Current export growth has slowed. Comparable four-quarter or two-half-year evidence does not justify an additional trajectory adjustment.
REV.anchor: Numerical starting score 9, net adjustment 0, then limited-history/Medium-confidence ceiling 8.
REV.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

DUR.reason: India Unit II headroom and the acquired Spanish retail channel provide real customer access. Pickled vegetables and olives have established demand, rather than a speculative new-category TAM.
DUR.contrary_evidence: Crop risk, customer/geographic concentration, price competition and integration constraints prevent a strong 7–8 runway grade.
DUR.anchor: 5–6 mixed runway, upper point. Funding costs are evaluated separately, not double-counted here.
DUR.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

CAP.reason: Opening operating capital of ₹343.2073 crore is reconciled. However, FY26 includes only a partial year of Spanish NOPAT, and acquisitions distort the aggregate incremental-return denominator.
CAP.contrary_evidence: India operating growth and use of existing capacity may create value. No mature unit/cohort cash-return evidence or clean three-/five-year incremental bridge proves it yet.
CAP.anchor: NS. Neither a closing-capital NOPAT yield nor hypothetical forecast ROIC substitutes for meaningful incremental returns.
CAP.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

CASH.reason: India CFO is negative throughout FY22–FY26. FY26 consolidated CFO of −₹57.2392 crore and cash capex of ₹51.1456 crore demonstrate funding intensity.
CASH.contrary_evidence: Most receivables are under six months old, and inventory growth has a stated seasonal/acquisition rationale. Neither establishes that book profits have been collected in cash.
CASH.anchor: 1–2 persistent, well-supported poor conversion, upper point. The eventual GQS ceiling of 5 applies, while missing CAP still leaves GQS NS.
CASH.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

BAL.reason: Net debt/core EBITDA is 3.30x and no audited undrawn facility is disclosed. The base cash bridge has a ₹9.65 crore deficit even with bank renewal assumed.
BAL.contrary_evidence: CRISIL BBB/Stable/A3+ and actual October conversion proceeds of ₹10.45548 crore support access. They prove neither current default nor unused rated capacity.
BAL.anchor: 3–4 material funding weakness, upper point. G3 is Hold, not an observed funding failure.
BAL.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

EXEC.reason: Indian exports and operating volumes grew, and the Spanish acquisitions were completed. Capacity expansion and international access are observable operating milestones.
EXEC.contrary_evidence: The earlier 30%+ growth aspiration was not met by 20.14% comparable FY26 export growth. Integration cash returns remain unseasoned.
EXEC.anchor: 5–6 mixed delivery, upper point. No bonus for future guidance.
EXEC.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

EARN.reason: Core EBITDA rose and parent PAT grew 25.82%. Reported consolidated PAT of ₹37.5096 crore includes ₹10.7753 crore of other income, including a ₹9.3048 crore FX gain.
EARN.contrary_evidence: Using current actual shares, reported-PAT EPS is ₹15.42 versus weighted reported ₹15.96; full conversion gives ₹14.53 before any return on proceeds. Operating-profit progress is real, but recurrence and per-share progress are uneven.
EARN.anchor: 5–6 mixed profit quality, lower point. Cash conversion is evaluated separately in CASH.
EARN.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

R.reason: Current October opening liquidity and five-year bank continuity are not verified. Base and bear cash deficits invalidate ordinary return estimates.
R.contrary_evidence: The bull path is nonnegative arithmetically and the separate rescue base returns about 4.0%, but neither is a supported ordinary financing case.
R.anchor: NS. Do not map hypothetical rescue financing or an unsupported bull return to the R schedule.
R.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

D.reason: The bear cash deficit is ₹54.41 crore. Hypothetical rescue dilution leaves roughly 81% terminal share-price loss, while full revolving-bank recall greatly exceeds the opening cash proxy.
D.contrary_evidence: Rated access and real manufacturing assets may mitigate timing. Forced-sale values and shareholder recovery are not established.
D.anchor: 1–2 severe permanent-loss/uncertain-recovery band, upper point. This is stress analysis, not a bankruptcy forecast.
D.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

P.reason: The price implies 24.45x reported PAT and 21.54x core EBITDA. At base operations, the 15% hurdle requires 17.51x terminal EBITDA after five years.
P.contrary_evidence: Rapid India growth and Spanish capacity could support higher profit. A comparable funded path and sustained cash normalization have not been proved.
P.anchor: 3–4 several optimistic assumptions must hold together, lower point.
P.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

L.reason: The theoretical ₹5 lakh, 5%-participation, 60-session test gives 0.8585 exit sessions and starts at L9. A real 600-share lot costs ₹226,200; ESM-I/ST restrictions matter.
L.contrary_evidence: All 60 sessions have trades. Recent 20-session whole-lot capacity gives 2.105 days for two lots and 3.158 for three; spread is unknown and one-sided circuits can stop execution.
L.anchor: Starting 9 is explicitly reduced by 3 points to 6 for lot granularity, recent capacity deterioration and ESM trade-for-trade/circuit risk. No executable size or suitability claim.
L.minimum_two_material_facts: Contained in reason with separately stated contrary evidence.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Freshara Agro Exports Limited is a fast-growing Indian gherkin exporter that has just become an India–Spain food manufacturer. The genuine operating expansion is not yet a demonstrated cash-generative compounder. FY26 consolidated profit was ₹37.51 crore, but operating cash flow was negative ₹57.24 crore and cash capex another ₹51.15 crore. The report explicitly says there are no undrawn operating borrowing facilities. At the 19 October close of ₹377, corrected equity value is ₹917.20 crore. [S1, S4, S8]

Classification: Hold — unresolved funding and incremental-capital evidence. CAP and R are NS, so BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS are all NS; no midpoint is substituted. This is not a fraud finding or an observed default. The first question is whether additional growth can be financed and converted into owner cash, not whether the acquisition expands the addressable market. A supported funding bridge and mature India/Spain capital-return evidence could reopen the assessment. [S1, S7]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: Freshara Agro Exports Limited, CIN L10306TN2023PLC165437, NSE Emerge FRESHARA, ISIN INE0SFW01015. The company was incorporated on 22 November 2023 following the predecessor partnership business established in 2015; listed on 24 October 2024. This is not a different similarly named agricultural company. Cutoff is 20 October 2026; official quote is 19 October close ₹377, last traded price ₹374. The statements use Accounting Standards (AS) under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021, not Ind AS. Consolidation under AS21 starts in FY26. [S1, S3, S8]

G1 Integrity Conditional: unmodified audit and disclosed related parties, with classification/reconciliation questions, no substantiated misuse conclusion. G2 Reliability Conditional: audited core figures are usable after explicit period and cash-flow corrections; new consolidation and some remuneration/working-capital disclosures need clarification. G3 Funding Hold — unresolved: no verified current headroom, negative cash generation and refinancing dependence. G4 Tradability Conditional: observable turnover, but ST/ESM-I, lots, circuits and unavailable spread/depth. G3 alone would not exclude quality scores; the separate missing CAP evidence does here. Historical statements/identity/quote confidence is Medium-to-High; forward funding, incremental returns and investment conclusion Low. Five analytical years end 19 October 2031; nominal pretax equity hurdle 15%, sensitivity 12%/18%, analytical capital-cost 13–17%. ₹5 lakh is only the prescribed liquidity reference, never a suitable allocation recommendation.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Factors: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 6, EARN 5; IAS-specific R NS, D 2, P 3, L 6. Every factor carries evidence, contrary facts, confidence and its anchor in the audit. BQS known contribution=1.00+1.00+0.96+0.60+0.20+0.32+0.48=4.56, coverage 88%; missing-CAP raw bound 4.68–5.76, not a score. GQS known=3.20+1.20+0.75+0.20=5.35, coverage 85%; raw missing bound 5.50–6.85. Persistent poor cash realization activates the 5.0 ceiling, but that ceiling cannot manufacture a complete GQS from missing CAP. [S1, S2, S3]

IAS known contribution=0.40+0.30+0.60=1.30, coverage 40%; Q is the exact final BQS, therefore also NS, and R is NS. Mechanical missing-factor bound 1.90–7.30 is not an estimate. No renormalization, rounding-before-classification or neutral defaults. Decimal arithmetic is exact; any eventual display uses half-up one decimal. All ranking flags are false because the point scores are incomplete, not simply because G3 is Hold. A one-point change in GOV/MOAT moves BQS 0.20, REV moves BQS 0.12/GQS 0.40, and CAP would move BQS 0.12/GQS 0.15 once supported; no sensitivity can resolve missing evidence.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Freshara sources vegetables through contract farming, processes and packs gherkins and other pickled vegetables for international institutional/private-label buyers, and now owns Spanish olive/pickle and retail-brand capabilities. The Indian value chain spans seed/agronomy support, farmer procurement, grading, processing, brining and packaging. Farmer relationships, product traceability and food-safety qualifications matter because a failed batch or shipment can destroy both inventory and buyer confidence. These are operating capabilities, not proof of pricing power. Management reports 4000+ farmers in 22 districts, exports to 40+ countries, and 34,885 MT dispatched in FY26. [S1, S3]

Unit I capacity is about 50 MT/day and Unit II 75–100 MT/day; reported utilization is approximately 100% and 60%, respectively. Gherkins were 82.8% of FY25 revenue. Spain subsidiaries Conservas Selectas Españolas SL and Gandin Invest SL were acquired on 20 January and 7 February 2026, respectively, after a court-approved process involving the Sarasa business. The first consolidated year captures only a short operating period, so annualizing the initial Spanish sales/profit is not a forecast. India sourcing into Spanish retail distribution may increase value added, but local labor, brand retention, integration and working capital make it more than a simple export-volume expansion. [S1, S5]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is a reliable sourcing-and-processing system: farmer relationships, food-safety compliance, customer qualification and consistent export execution. Switching a qualified supplier has practical costs. However, these are contestable processes. Reitzel's primary description also emphasizes contract farming, traceability and export manufacturing; its presence contradicts any suggestion that Freshara's network is unique. The historical top 10 customer share was 42% and Russia exposure 23.23% in FY24. Current exact customer/geographic concentration was not established, so those percentages are not carried forward as FY26 facts. [S1, S3, S12]

Three qualitative comparators are used without borrowing their multiples: Reitzel is closest in pickles/contract farming but privately held; ADF Foods has more branded ethnic-food/distribution economics; Tasty Bite is a prepared-foods manufacturer with different products and customer relationships. None is a clean listed pure-play valuation match. Freshara's management market-share claims are not independently verified. MOAT 5 recognizes a useful but contestable operating position; higher scores require demonstrated retention, pricing resilience and excess unit returns through a cycle, not just certification logos or a large food-industry TAM.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The comparable India export series is ₹111.28 cr FY22, ₹125.99 cr FY23, ₹193.79 cr FY24, ₹250.64 cr FY25 and ₹301.11 cr FY26. FY24 combines contiguous partnership and company income periods; the ₹71.31 cr successor stub is not a full-year base. The preferred available three-year FY23–FY26 CAGR is 33.70%; the four-year cross-check is 28.26%, while a genuine five-year series is unavailable. The numerical REV starting point is 9, net trajectory adjustment 0, then an 8 ceiling for limited comparable history and Medium confidence. FY26 comparable export growth 20.14% is still strong but slower than the three-year CAGR. [S1, S2, S3]

Reported FY26 parent operating revenue ₹313.53 cr includes ₹12.42 cr of operating income/incentives, against recast FY25 ₹254.31 cr including ₹3.68 cr. Consolidated ₹342.29 cr adds around ₹29.14 cr Spanish revenue less ₹0.39 cr elimination. Comparing that total with prior standalone revenue produces 34.59% growth but mixes perimeter; it is not the underlying rate scored. Production/dispatch expansion supports real demand, yet price, currency and mix contributions are not separately reconciled, so nominal sales growth is not described as pure volume growth. No additional small-base or acquisition penalty is applied after fixing the basis.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Base-case geographic revenues grow from India ₹350 cr plus Spain ₹150 cr in year 1 to ₹532 cr plus ₹258 cr in year 5. The Spain starting runrate is deliberately below mechanical annualization of its first two-month contribution; subsequent growth assumes qualification, retention and routing through India. A physical sensitivity takes 34,885 MT dispatch and ₹313.53 cr India operating revenue as a mixed-product realization proxy, assumes 5% annual realization growth and 300 production days. At the upper 150 MT/day plant capacity, year 5 base requires about 3% debottlenecking; bull requires roughly 24% more throughput or a richer mix. These are not commissioned funded additions. [S1, S5]

Base capex totals ₹69 cr and base operating working capital rises from ₹245.05 cr to ₹402.90 cr despite its ratio falling from 71.6% of audited sales to 51% of year 5 sales. The cash bridge still fails in years 2–3. Existing physical headroom is not free growth when inventories and receivables have to be financed. Closing normalized NOPAT/capital is 10.21%, below the 13–17% analytical capital-cost range, but it is a partial-year, mixed-perimeter snapshot and is not scored as incremental ROI. The acquisition opening capital and mature cohort returns are not reconciled; three-/five-year incremental ROIC is NM and no evidenced unit-economics substitute exists. CAP remains NS, not a neutral 5 or an automatic low score.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The company has delivered a listing, Indian plant expansion, sustained export growth and completed Spanish acquisitions. Those outcomes support EXEC 6, although reported comparable FY26 export growth 20.14% did not meet the earlier 30%+ growth aspiration and the integration has not yet earned a full-year cash-return record. Forecast Spain margins, ₹500 cr capacity-linked revenue potential and procurement synergies are management claims, not achieved results. The October allotment is an actual financing event and is credited; the remaining warrants are optional. [S1, S4, S5, S6]

The FY26 audit is unmodified, including disclosed reliance on subsidiary auditors. The annual report says IPO proceeds were used for working capital ₹56 cr, capex ₹8.7997 cr, general corporate ₹7.591 cr and issue costs ₹3 cr. Related-party rents total ₹0.684 cr. Disclosed remuneration to three directors totals ₹1.8 cr, whereas a narrower directors/sitting-fee P&L line is ₹1.028 cr; a classification or timing reconciliation is needed, not an allegation of concealed diversion. The three named promoter directors held 59.68% at March; the report separately lists 10,680,000 promoter-group shares and 315,600 public shares under lock-in. Those dated facts do not establish current post-conversion free float or pledge status. GOV 5 reflects mixed adequate conduct and disclosure questions without an integrity-failure override.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The embedded six-row history separates predecessor, combined FY24, recast FY25, FY26 parent and first-year consolidated accounts. FY26 consolidated sales ₹342.29 cr, other income ₹10.78 cr, PAT ₹37.51 cr and core EBITDA excluding other income ₹50.30 cr imply 14.69% operating EBITDA margin. FX gain ₹9.30 cr is a major component of non-operating income; removing all other income and applying 25% tax yields a recurring after-finance profit proxy ₹29.23 cr, not an audited restatement. Current-share reported EPS is ₹15.42, fully converted ₹14.53 before any return on optional proceeds. Gross margin remains ND because cost categories are not consistently split across years. [S1, S2, S3, S4]

FY26 consolidated CFO −₹57.2392 cr plus investing −₹50.8063 cr and financing ₹88.5763 cr reconcile the ₹19.4692 cr cash decline. Cash capex ₹51.1456 cr gives FCF −₹108.3848 cr. The parent's printed positive CFO is demonstrably a sign/presentation issue: negative ₹9.4275 cr before tax less ₹11.1289 cr tax implies negative ₹20.5565 cr within rounding, consistent with the cash bridge. FY25 annual comparative CFO −₹1.7680 cr supersedes original −₹0.1159 cr after noncurrent asset reclassification. These differences are disclosed rather than silently mixed. [S1, S2, S15]

Consolidated inventory ₹143.56 cr and receivables ₹149.92 cr dominate capital. Most receivables are under 6 months but balances are subject to confirmation, not independently validated collection. Debt ₹179.62 cr includes current term maturities and lease obligations once; net debt/core EBITDA 3.30 x and EBIT/finance cost 6.03 x. Cash ₹13.41 cr includes ₹2.95 cr short-dated deposits, excluded from core available cash conservatively and restored in sensitivity. Annual note 22 expressly discloses no undrawn operating facility. CRISIL's ₹175 cr rated capacity mixes funded, nonfunded/proposed amounts and stale utilization; it is not spare cash. GST/TDS disputes ₹2.5021 cr are contingent and stress-tested, not falsely described as adjudicated debt.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Use 2.4329 cr actual shares after 7 October, not the stale master 2.34992 cr. At ₹377, market cap ₹917.2033 cr and dated-balance EV ₹1083.4039 cr imply 24.45 x reported PAT, 21.54 x core EBITDA and 3.17 x sales. EV and net-debt ratios use March debt/cash with October shares or FY26 earnings, respectively; neither establishes current October cash, debt or leverage. A separate dated pro-forma book bridge starts with March equity and adjusts only the known October conversion. Of ₹9.7272 cr March warrant deposits, ₹3.48516 cr now belongs to converted issued-holder common equity; only ₹6.24204 cr remains attributable to unconverted warrants. Adding the new ₹10.45548 cr cash once gives ₹179.37214 cr common book and 5.1134 x price/book. This is not verified October book equity. Income and enterprise-value approaches both matter because capex and working-capital absorption make a headline P/E inadequate. No forced peer average is imported. [S1, S4, S8, S10]

Ordinary bear/base/bull models contain full annual revenues, margins, taxes, interest, capex, working capital, debt, cash and shares. Bear/base have peak deficits ₹54.41 cr/₹9.65 cr. Bull stays positive only under ambitious cash-ratio improvement and assumed bank continuity. All ordinary investor IRRs are null without verified funding. A separate rescue illustration raises equity at 25% discount with 3% issue cost whenever cash would fall below ₹5 cr: base return about 3.98%, bear −28.06%, bull's conditional arithmetic 21.02%. Rescue capital is not claimed available. No buy-under price is presented from an unfunded ordinary model. [S1, S4, S7]

The 15% hurdle requires ₹758.28 terminal price. At base operations, this needs 17.51 x terminal EBITDA versus the 11 x base assumption, while funded execution remains unresolved. A nine-cell growth/multiple sensitivity, cash/warrant/bank-call/contingency sensitivities, 12/15/18% hurdles and execution costs are embedded. An independent FCFF DCF tests 13–17% discount, 3–5% terminal growth and explicit 15% terminal incremental ROIC/reinvestment. Its contingent values ₹45.63–₹116.22 are not financeable fair-value recommendations; the gap versus optimistic exit multiples shows terminal-expectation risk.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
A plausible loss chain is crop/freight pressure and buyer competition reducing margin, inventory taking longer to clear, collections slowing, banks tightening renewals, then discounted equity or forced asset sales. The linked bear case uses ₹380 cr first-year sales, 9% EBITDA margin, 74% operating WC/sales and 9.5% interest, not an isolated multiple haircut. It produces a ₹54.41 cr cash deficit even with continuing revolving facilities assumed. Hypothetical rescue then dilutes shareholders and leaves about 81% terminal price loss; without rescue, recovery is unknown, not an ordinary negative-IRR investment path. [S1, S7]

Full withdrawal of ₹127.63 cr revolving/export bank principal is separately stressed against the opening cash proxy, as is ₹2.5021 cr contingent-tax payment and ₹10 cr unobserved post-March cash burn. Nominal access to rated facilities or optional warrant conversion cannot solve a simultaneous stress without verified terms. This supports D 2 severe impairment/uncertain recovery, while G3 remains Hold rather than an observed default. Asset salvage values and Spanish insolvency-title/realization proceeds are not asserted. The contrary case is continued rated access, actual October cash and retained customers; it must show collections and debt service, not just reported earnings.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold price outcome in five years requires 37.97% annual appreciation; tenfold requires 58.49%, before costs and personal taxes. From ₹377, terminal prices are ₹1885 and ₹3770. Even at 20 x exit P/E and no further dilution, required EPS is ₹94.25/₹188.50 and PAT approximately ₹229.30 cr/₹458.60 cr. At 10% net margin the implied revenue is ₹2293 cr/₹4586 cr versus ₹342 cr audited consolidated sales and ₹790 cr/₹995 cr base/bull year 5 scenarios. The full arithmetic is embedded. [S1, S4, S8]

These outcomes would require several successes together: much larger capacity and customer access, durable profitable Spanish integration, dramatically better cash conversion, financed reinvestment and limited dilution. A larger headline TAM or ₹500 cr management Spain capacity claim does not establish that chain. Multiple expansion alone cannot be called business compounding. No evidence-backed 5×/10× case or compounder designation is supported now; the test is an explicit scale-and-capital requirement, not a probability forecast.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before investment ranking, obtain a current consolidated cash/debt statement, lender-sanction and utilization schedules with actual undrawn eligibility, renewal/covenant conditions, borrowing-base haircuts and debt maturities. Reconcile acquisition opening assets/liabilities and debt, cash paid, inherited inventory/receivables and integration cash costs. Require at least a full operating-year India/Spain return and collection bridge, with customer cohorts or meaningful incremental capital returns. Positive EBITDA alone does not clear CAP or R. [S1, S7]

At each half-year, track comparable India export revenue separately from incentives, currency and Spain; inventory ageing, subsequent collections, CFO after tax and cash capex; debt service and promoter/warrant dilution. Reconcile the parent's CFO sign and director remuneration line. Warning thresholds for review, not automatic sell orders: another profitable period with negative operating cash, net debt/core EBITDA above 3.5 x, meaningful AR ageing beyond 6 months or renewal restrictions. Verify warrant exercise/expiry by 12 September 2027, actual shares and current ESM/lot status. Thesis strengthens only with funded growth and repeatable returns; it fails if capital needs are repeatedly funded by dilution without improved cash economics.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Fast underlying growth is real, but growth quality cannot be completed without incremental-capital evidence and investment attractiveness cannot be scored without a supported funding path. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS. There is no governance-avoid override, observed default classification, buy price, position-size recommendation or trade instruction. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is methodological only. [S1, S3, S7]

At ₹377, one 600-share lot costs ₹226,200. Two lots cost ₹452,400 and fit within ₹5 lakh; three cost ₹678,600 and exceed it. The exact ₹5 lakh continuous capacity is kept separate: 0.8585 sessions at 5% of the conservative 60 day turnover measure, versus 1.6011 on 20 days. Discrete two/three-lot average capacity is 0.736/1.104 sessions on 60 days and 2.105/3.158 on 20 days. For a whole-session planning display, those average-capacity figures round up to 1/2 sessions over 60 days and 3/4 over 20 days. They are not an execution forecast. At 2% recent participation, the two/three-lot estimates stretch to 13.33/20 sessions because most sessions cannot absorb a whole-lot. ESM-I/ST trade-for-trade and 5% bands, unknown spread and potential one-sided circuits can defeat all these historical averages. G4 Conditional and L 6 reflect those constraints, not guaranteed execution. [S8, S9, S10, S11]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence is the SEBI prospectus, NSE-hosted annual reports/filings, CRISIL's dated rating rationale and official daily NSE archives/master. Financial history, normalization, opening claim register, annual cash/debt/share models, all sensitivity rows, capacity proxy, 60 session market observations and source URLs/hashes are embedded in the canonical JSON. Reproduction scripts accompany it; file paths are supplementary, not substitutes for inputs. Retrieval on 21 October does not admit post-cutoff results. Undated peer pages supply only qualitative context; no unsupported peer financial valuation is used. [S1–S15]

Key limitations: no verified October liquidity bridge or bank commitments; incomplete acquisition capital flow; short Spanish track record; no harmonized gross margin or meaningful 3/5 year incremental ROIC; current exact customer concentration, post-conversion free float/pledges and bid/ask depth unverified. A blocked local CRISIL download is not represented as a valid cached rating document; the browser-read primary page was used. Raw issuer PDFs/text and shareholding documents are intentionally excluded from private Library backups because they may contain unnecessary personal identifiers; URLs, hashes and identifier-free financial extracts remain. Disclosures of uncertainty change scoreability and gates rather than being hidden after a precise-looking target price.

liquidity.interpretation: The exact ₹500,000 continuous test is not a feasible whole-lot position. Two 600-share lots cost ₹452,400 and fit within the reference budget; three cost ₹678,600 and exceed it. Neither is an allocation recommendation. Whole-lot capacity is floor(volume × participation / 600), computed separately for every session and then averaged. All 60 valid market archives and all 60 issuer trading rows are observed.

limitations: No current October bank statements, borrowing availability or pro-forma acquisition opening balance bridge; opening cash proxy is not current fact.
